title: He fought for the wrong king…
paragraphs:
He fought for the wrong king…
…and still got called by the right one.
Read that again.
Because most of us think one wrong allegiance disqualifies us forever.

Amasa didn’t just make a mistake.
He chose a side.
The wrong side.

He stood under Absalom’s banner—against David, God’s anointed king. Not neutral. Not confused. He was fully aligned in rebellion. When the dust settled and Absalom fell, Amasa should have been remembered as a traitor. Disqualified. Forgotten.
But then something happened that doesn’t make sense unless you understand grace.
David called for him.

Not to punish him.
Not to shame him publicly.
But to restore him.
In 2 Samuel 19:13, David says, “Are you not my bone and my flesh?”—and then offers him leadership.
Let that sit heavy.
The man who stood against the king… was invited back into the king’s service.

That’s not strategy.
That’s mercy.
And this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because Amasa is not just a character in Scripture.
He’s a mirror.
Where have you been quietly standing against God while still claiming His name?

Not loudly.
Not publicly.
But in the hidden places.

Delayed obedience.
Private compromise.
That habit you defend in your mind but wouldn’t dare confess out loud.
That pride that whispers, “I know better.”

You still show up.
You still pray sometimes.
You still wear the label.
But your heart?
Divided.
James 1:8 says a double-minded man is unstable in all his ways. Not just some. All.
So let me ask you—honestly:
Are you loyal… or just familiar with God?
Do you follow Him… or just orbit Him?
This is where many believers live—not in open rebellion, but in quiet resistance. And it’s more dangerous because it feels normal.
Here’s the AHA moment:
You don’t have to hate God to stand against Him. You just have to choose yourself over Him consistently.
That’s it.
Sin doesn’t always look like defiance. Sometimes it looks like delay. Like “later, Lord.” Like partial surrender.
And partial surrender is still resistance.
Romans 5:10 says we were enemies of God before reconciliation. Not just lost. Not just confused. Enemies.
That means before Christ, we weren’t just wandering—we were aligned against Him.
Just like Amasa.
But here’s where grace breaks in.
While we were still sinners—still misaligned, still choosing self—Christ died for us (Romans 5:8). Not after we cleaned up. Not after we switched sides.
While we were still on the wrong side.
That’s the Gospel.

Jesus didn’t wait for loyalty.
He moved toward rebellion.
On the cross, He absorbed the full weight of our divided hearts, our hidden compromises, our silent “no’s” to God—and He paid for it in full.
Not to excuse sin.
But to destroy its power.
So now the call is not just “be better.”
It’s repent.
Turn.
Leave the false allegiance.
Because grace is not permission to stay the same—it is power to become new.
Here’s the conviction line:
Some people want the benefits of the Kingdom without bowing to the King. That is not Christianity—that is self-deception.
Let that cut clean.

Because Jesus is not just Savior.
He is Lord.
And Lord means He leads. Fully.
Identity check:

You are not a divided soul trying to manage sin.
You are called to be a redeemed son or daughter, fully surrendered, fully alive in Christ.

Not half in.
Not occasionally obedient.
Not selectively surrendered.
All in.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:
The areas you refuse to surrender are the areas where you still believe you are a better king than Jesus.
That’s the real battle.
But hear this—clearly, deeply:
Just like Amasa, you are still being called.

Not because you were loyal.
But because He is merciful.

Not because you earned it.
But because Jesus paid for it.
Ephesians 2:4–5 says God is rich in mercy, and even when we were dead in sin, He made us alive with Christ.
Alive.

Not tolerated.
Not barely accepted.
Alive.
But you cannot stay in rebellion and claim resurrection.
You must respond.
So here it is—simple, but not easy:

Bring your divided heart to Jesus.
Name the compromise.
Confess the hidden allegiance.
Turn from it.
He is not waiting to reject you.
He is calling you back.
Right now.
If this is hitting deeper than you expected… that’s not coincidence. That’s conviction. And conviction is not condemnation—it’s an invitation.
Not surface-level faith. Real transformation. Take your time with them. Let God meet you there.
But don’t stop at reading.
Respond.
And stay ready…
Because the next message might expose what you’ve been avoiding.
